# The encoder ceiling — what `frozen EV` is failing against

Built on branch `encoder/ceiling` 2026-09-10; **merged into `main` at `5592390`** and placed in the
deck at `9630379`.

Priya: "should we do a similar per-session refit with the encoder analysis as we did with the
decoder?" Yes — and more than for the decoder, because the frozen encoder's score had no ceiling.

**Every number in this document is regenerated by
`scripts/prelim_numbers_encoder_ceiling.py`** and was last pulled 2026-09-10 at
`ENC_CEILING_REPEATS = 32`. An earlier pull at 8 is the source of any figure quoted elsewhere that
disagrees in the third decimal; nothing in the reading changes between them.

---

## The problem

`frozen EV` is an R², and acutely it is **−0.388** post-cue. That says "worse than predicting the
mean" and nothing about what was achievable in that session. `EV after rescale` frees the AMPLITUDE
only — and `_enc_terms` warns in its own docstring that a large rescaling gain means amplitude only
when the rescaled value is HIGH, because a code that is simply gone also recovers a lot under
rescaling. That ambiguity forced the withdrawal of the "half amplitude, half shape" reading on
2026-09-10.

> **WHAT "EXPLAINED VARIANCE" IS THE VARIANCE OF, because the name invites the wrong reading.**
> Priya, 2026-09-10: "if the encoder is literally an average per position, we're asking how much of
> all the trials the AVERAGE (binned) per-position activity explains?" The first half is right and
> the second half is not. The encoder IS the per-position average of the binned component activity.
> But the score is computed MEAN against MEAN: `M` and `P` are both 6 x features matrices of
> per-position mean patterns, centred across positions, and the denominator is `sum M^2` — the
> BETWEEN-POSITION variance of the measured means. Trial-to-trial variance never enters it. So the
> number answers "how much of the measured position-to-position pattern does the template's
> position-to-position pattern reproduce", not "how much of the trial variance is explained"; a
> trial-level R2 would be far lower, because single-trial noise is large and is excluded here by
> construction. It also means the CEILING's shortfall from 1.0 is entirely sampling noise in the
> half-session means — which is why halving the trials lowers it, and why the size-matched arm was
> needed at all.

## What centring across positions removes — and what it does not

Priya, 2026-09-10: *"I'm not getting the sum of M squared being the between-position signal — even
if there were patterns at different positions that averaged out with global session mean (say,
inverted activity patterns), we should still see between-position signal. This is literally just
summing the square of the 6x380 matrix?"*

Yes, literally — but of `M` **after** `M = M − M.mean(0)`, and that one line is what earns the name.
The claim is an identity, not a gloss, and it is pinned in
`tests/test_encoder_ceiling.py` so the prose cannot drift from the code.

**1. The identity.** With `n = 6` positions, after centring,

```
sum(M**2)  ==  6 * sum_over_features( Var_across_positions(feature) )
```

exactly — because the sum of squares down a column of a mean-zero vector IS `n` times its variance.
Nothing about trials enters; trial-to-trial noise was averaged away before `M` was formed.

**2. Every contrast the encoder is scored on is untouched.** Centring subtracts the SAME row from
all six rows, so `M[i] − M[j]` is invariant for every pair. The encoder is only ever asked to
reproduce differences between positions, and centring changes none of them.

**3. The inverted-pattern case, which looks like a counterexample and is not.** Three positions at
`+x` and three at `−x` have a mean across positions of exactly zero, so centring subtracts nothing
and the signal is retained **in full** — sum of squares unchanged to 1e-12. "Averages out with the
global session mean" describes a pattern that is the SAME at every position, which carries no
position information by definition; not one that is opposite at different positions, which carries
the most position information six rows can carry.

**4. The only thing it kills** is a pattern identical at every position, however large: six rows of
100 go from a sum of squares of 2.1e7 to 1.3e-25. That is a session-wide shift in F0 or SNR, which
the encoder is not being asked to predict and which would otherwise inflate the denominator and make
every EV look better than it is.

**5. It does not remove GAIN.** Centring removes an ADDITIVE common offset, not a MULTIPLICATIVE
one: scaling every position by 0.4 scales the centred matrix by 0.4 and its sum of squares by 0.16.
If centring removed gain there would be nothing for the amplitude factor `a` to fit, and this
document's whole amplitude-vs-shape split would be empty.

## Construction

A refit encoder must be **cross-validated or it is 1.0 by construction** — ridge on a one-hot
position design reduces to the per-position mean, so predicting a session's own means from
themselves is an identity. Splitting the trials makes it a prediction. Three arms, all scoring the
SAME half-session means, **32** random splits, both orderings averaged:

| arm | reference | holds constant |
|---|---|---|
| **ceiling** | the other half of the same session | — |
| **frozen (matched)** | an equally sized draw from the pre-stroke pool | training-set size |
| **frozen (all pre)** | the whole pre-stroke pool | nothing; this is the encoder as actually used |

**Read `ceiling − frozen (matched)`.** Only that pair holds size constant, so only it isolates "the
template came from other sessions". And read it against its own PRE value, not against zero.

### How many splits — measured, after it was asked

Priya, 2026-09-10: "how did we decide on 8 splits?" It had been a guess, and nobody had checked.
Re-running PS92_0606 post-cue under 20 seeds:

| repeats | 1 | 2 | 4 | 8 | 16 | **32** | 64 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| seed SD | 0.147 | 0.133 | 0.076 | 0.045 | 0.038 | **0.025** | 0.017 |

Falling as 1/√r, as it must. **Eight was adequate** — a per-session SD of 0.045 pools to roughly
0.007–0.011 at the epoch level, about 5% of the acute effect — but the splits themselves cost almost
nothing beside `_collect_7`, which is memoised and dominates the runtime. `ENC_CEILING_REPEATS = 32`
cuts the seed-dependence 1.8× for no measurable time. Moving 8 → 32 changed the pooled post-cue
gaps by −0.000 / −0.005 / −0.016 / +0.003 across pre / acute / subacute / chronic.

## Why the matched arm was required

Without it the pre-cue window was uninterpretable — frozen EV **0.330** against a ceiling of
**0.090**, a frozen arm beating its own ceiling, which is impossible for a real ceiling and is a
fact about the construction rather than the data. The unmatched frozen arm scores against a
reference pooled over ~10 sessions while the ceiling's reference is half a session.

Matching removes the asymmetry, and the inversion goes with it **in all three windows**: ceiling ≥
matched at pre-stroke everywhere.

## Results — SHAPE ONLY (after rescale)

All three arms are scored after rescale, so amplitude is out of every number. Raw scores at these
amplitudes are dominated by the encoder not being allowed to rescale: with PERFECT shape and only a
scale mismatch, `R² = 1 − (1−a)²/a²`, which is exactly 0.000 at a = 0.5 and **−2.13** at the
a = 0.361 observed acutely. A raw ceiling-minus-matched gap therefore reports amplitude and calls it
template mismatch, because the ceiling's two halves have matched amplitude by construction while the
matched frozen arm does not.

### Post-cue (new boundaries; chronic = 12 sessions, 3 animals)

| epoch | ceiling | matched | gap | Δ vs pre | template captures | a (matched) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| pre | 0.706 | 0.429 | 0.276 | — | 61% | 0.749 |
| **acute** | 0.568 | 0.100 | 0.468 | **+0.192** | **18%** | **0.286** |
| subacute | 0.631 | 0.226 | 0.405 | +0.128 | 36% | 0.527 |
| chronic | 0.778 | 0.315 | 0.463 | **+0.186** | 41% | 0.745 |

**AMPLITUDE RECOVERS; SHAPE DOES NOT.** The fitted scale goes 0.286 → 0.527 → **0.745** against a
pre-stroke 0.749 — back to baseline. The shape mismatch goes +0.192 → +0.128 → **+0.186** — flat,
and if anything worse at chronic than at subacute. An earlier version of this document reported the
mismatch as monotonically recovering (+0.666, +0.309, +0.181); those were RAW scores and what was
recovering in them was the amplitude.

> **WHICH `a`.** The column above is the amplitude the MATCHED arm fitted, which is the one to read
> beside `matched`. The unmatched, as-actually-used frozen arm fits a different and larger one —
> 0.943 / **0.361** / 0.677 / 0.947. That second number is the one quoted when explaining why the
> RAW frozen EV is confounded (`R² = 1 − (1−a)²/a² = −2.13` at a = 0.361), because there the arm
> being described is the unmatched one. Both are correct in their own place and they have been
> confused once; `scripts/prelim_numbers_encoder_ceiling.py` now prints both, labelled.

**THE PRE-STROKE GAP IS 0.276 AND IS NOT AN EFFECT** — the cost of a template coming from other
sessions at equal training-set size, with no lesion involved. Same phenomenon the matched frozen
DECODER arm exposed, where matching flipped its pre-stroke gap from −0.073 to +0.090.

| epoch | ceiling | matched | gap | Δ vs pre | captures | a (matched) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| pre | 0.749 | 0.474 | 0.275 | — | 63% | 0.784 |
| acute | 0.606 | 0.238 | 0.368 | +0.092 | 39% | 0.561 |
| subacute | 0.681 | 0.251 | 0.430 | +0.155 | 37% | 0.563 |

Milder acutely than post-cue, and the same non-recovery of shape with amplitude back at baseline.

### Pre-cue — self-consistent now, but weak throughout

| epoch | ceiling | matched | gap | Δ vs pre | captures | a (matched) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| pre | 0.365 | 0.172 | 0.193 | — | 47% | 0.429 |
| acute | 0.304 | 0.059 | 0.245 | +0.052 | 19% | 0.231 |
| subacute | 0.261 | 0.073 | 0.188 | **−0.005** | 28% | 0.243 |
| chronic | 0.334 | 0.063 | 0.271 | +0.078 | 19% | 0.242 |

The inversion is gone — ceiling exceeds matched at every epoch — but the ceiling is 0.365 at its best
against 0.71–0.75 for the other two windows, and the amplitude factor never recovers (0.242 chronic
against 0.429 pre-stroke). Contrasts here are small differences between small numbers; treat as
suggestive only. **The subacute Δ changed SIGN between the 8-split and 32-split pulls** (+0.017 to
−0.005), which is exactly the fragility this section warns about, and is the clearest argument for
having measured the split count rather than guessing it.

## Per position — and this is the finding

Post-cue, shape (after rescale). `ceiling` = what that position's own trials can predict; `match` =
what the pre-stroke template gets; `frac` = the second over the first.

| position | pre ceil / frac | acute ceil / frac | subacute frac | chronic frac | Δ ceiling acute |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| near ipsi | 0.740 / 0.67 | 0.584 / 0.28 | 0.41 | 0.33 | −0.156 |
| near middle | 0.462 / 0.31 | 0.455 / 0.22 | 0.19 | 0.13 | −0.007 |
| near contra | 0.731 / 0.63 | 0.616 / 0.27 | 0.47 | 0.53 | −0.115 |
| **far ipsi** | 0.629 / 0.56 | 0.306 / 0.22 | 0.34 | 0.37 | **−0.323** |
| **far middle** | 0.721 / 0.63 | 0.451 / 0.42 | 0.37 | 0.50 | **−0.270** |
| **far contra** | 0.628 / 0.55 | **0.626** / **0.01** | 0.34 | 0.28 | **−0.002** |

**FAR-CONTRA LOSES NO STRUCTURE AND LOSES ITS TEMPLATE ENTIRELY.** Ceiling 0.626 acutely against
0.628 pre-stroke, a change of −0.002 — its own trials predict each other exactly as well as before —
while the pre-stroke template captures 1% of that, down from 55%. The positions that lose CEILING are
the flanking ones: far-ipsi −0.323 and far-middle −0.270.

**THE FRACTION IS CLIPPED TO [0, 1], AND AT FAR-CONTRA ACUTELY THAT CLIP HIDES A SIGN.** The
underlying matched EV there is **−0.060**: the pre-stroke template is further from that position's
measured pattern than predicting zero would be. Per-position scores use the session-GLOBAL scale
factor, fitted to a session the other five positions dominate, so at a position whose amplitude has
collapsed that factor is simply the wrong one — which the pooled after-rescale score, free to choose
a = 0, can never be. Quote the fraction (0.55 → 0.01); do not quote the clip as though the number
underneath it were positive. An earlier version of this table printed **−0.11** in the fraction
column, which was neither the fraction nor the current value of the EV.

**This converges with the frozen-vs-refit DECODER arm**, which found refitting recovers 34% of
far-contra's acute deficit and only 9% / 11% at far-ipsi / far-middle. Two analyses, opposite
directions of fit, same dissociation: far-contra's code is DISPLACED, its neighbours' codes are
DEGRADED. The pooled "~28% of structure lost" figure averages those two different things and should
not be quoted without the split.

Figures: `epoch_11cpos_encoder_ceiling_by_position_*` (the ceiling) and
`epoch_11cfrac_encoder_captured_by_position_*` (the fraction). The fraction is dropped rather than
drawn where the ceiling is below 0.10, since a ratio to a near-zero denominator reads as a result.

## Still to do on this branch

1. ~~Deck placement~~ **DONE** at `9630379`: `11c`, `11cpos` and `11cfrac` each have `_EPOCH` entries
   across six arms. **Nothing on the share shows them yet** — the grant/epoch re-render has not run
   since they landed.
2. **Intervals on the derived gap.** The bars carry hierarchical-bootstrap intervals; the
   `ceiling − matched` difference is computed per epoch from the pooled values and has none. Every
   `Δ vs pre` in this document is therefore a point estimate, and the post-cue subacute value
   (+0.128) sits close enough to acute and chronic (+0.192, +0.186) that "flat" is a reading of
   three points without error bars.
3. **A per-COMPONENT ceiling does not exist and may be the interesting one.** The score is pooled
   over all 6 positions × 380 features; the only breakdown is per POSITION. Restricting both sums to
   one component's 4 sub-bin columns would give 95 numbers per session — "which areas carry the
   displaced code and which carry the degraded one". Two obstacles: 24 cells per component is noisy,
   and 95 components is a multiple-comparison problem the marks machinery is not set up for. It
   would want grouping by Allen area rather than 95 independent bars.
